feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by concrete scope indicators. It reads clearly overall, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and limited outcome-focused evidence beyond activity and scale.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression within NACo into senior digital strategy, platform, analytics, and multimedia ownership.  
- Good credibility signals: named employer, measurable scope (10,000+ pages, 3.5M page views, 50+ publishers), and modern tools/platforms.  
- Broad but coherent skill set across web modernization, governance, analytics, AI-enabled search, and content operations.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more results/impact metrics: include outcomes such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption improvements, campaign performance, or search success metrics.  
- Reduce duplication across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; consolidate to sharpen structure and save space.  
- Fix stylistic consistency issues: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s”; serial comma use is inconsistent (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. other lists); “French (A2/Learning)” is awkward—use “French (A2, learning).” No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the first sentence and make the value proposition more direct: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years leading web platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with stronger outcome-oriented phrasing such as “leading modernization of” or “scaling.”
- Consider adding one concrete scope marker from recent roles for impact, e.g., “10,000+ page websites,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ publishers.”
- Streamline the second sentence to reduce list fatigue: group related areas (e.g., “web modernization, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled search/content experiences”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled search and content discovery.”
- The subtitle already signals leadership; avoid repeating too many broad capability labels here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but the section is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, concise noun phrases and prioritize strategic/enterprise-level strengths over operational wording.
- Replace “Multi-channel communications operations” with “Multi-channel communications leadership” to better match seniority.
- Consider this version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space is tight, shorten “AI-enabled search and content experiences” to “AI-enabled search and content discovery” for sharper specificity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it high-level and avoid tool-specific language already covered elsewhere.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with multiple summary sections; consider keeping just “Public-sector advocacy communications.”
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer currently repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense for a closing section. Tightening wording and emphasizing outcomes or distinct scope will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and make the section feel curated.
- Standardize verb tense and structure; use parallel phrasing like “Built,” “Developed,” “Launched,” “Produced.”
- Trim technical stacking in the AI project and foreground user/business value: “improved discovery of legislative content.”
- Consider shortening each item to one crisp line and, where possible, add scale or audience impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI Hybrid Search,” the microsite, and the advocacy video series closely overlap with current NACo bullets; keep only if reframed as selected project highlights rather than repeating role duties.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” feels most additive because it introduces conference display and archival storytelling not stated elsewhere.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level impact, transformation, and 2–3 signature outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, web modernization, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for enterprise communications platforms.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4 impact-led bullets; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one operations bullet.
- Shift phrasing from duties to outcomes: “Built”/“Launched”/“Designed”/“Standardized” rather than “Consult”/“Advise”/“Deliver.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: number of sites/pages/users, toolkit downloads, publishing teams supported, reduction in publishing time, search success gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search initiative” and “campaign/storytelling experiences” duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the detail.
- “Governance, usability, workflows and analytics” overlaps with the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize new consulting remit or post-director contributions.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia operations, and budget oversight across web, email, social, and video.”
- Make bullets more results-led and parallel: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: quantify team size, budget, reporting improvements, production volume, cost savings from the in-house studio, or engagement gains from email/social.
- Tighten vague phrasing: replace “strengthened digital operations” with specifics such as governance model, publishing SLAs, editorial calendar system, or cross-department workflow adopted.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo entries unless framed here as building organizational production infrastructure.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Tighten it around executional leadership, cross-team coordination, and any measurable channel growth or workflow improvements.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social, and video, coordinating editorial and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine related bullets and make outcomes clearer: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Sharpen the video bullet to show impact: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with stronger ownership if accurate: “Improved editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams.” Add metrics if available: open rates, production volume, turnaround time, or audience growth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video” and “weekly video updates” also appear in the prior NACo role and footer project list; avoid repeating the same accomplishment in similar terms.
- “Strengthened workflows/editorial planning” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this version more execution-focused than strategic.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more specific, senior-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial systems, publishing standards & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “content planning” for “content operations” or “publishing standards” to better match recent leadership scope.
- Keep terms parallel and concise; avoid mixing broad strategy with tactical phrasing.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable proof points for recent roles rather than this skills block.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” repeat language already used in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is close to “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize platform leadership and recent, higher-impact technical capabilities rather than exhaustive software naming.

Suggested edit:

- Remove lower-priority or older platform names unless job-relevant; keep Drupal first given the recent 10,000+ page migration and current consulting work.
- Drop “jQuery” from this topline section unless specifically required; it dates the profile and is better suited to Technical + IT.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Enterprise CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” is already repeated in Technical + IT; avoid mirroring the same list here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. This item should either add level/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show depth and recency: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, prioritize strongest/current tools first and de-emphasize lighter-use platforms: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages” (drop GitHub Pages unless used meaningfully in recent work)
- Consider adding proficiency cues only if accurate: “Drupal (advanced) • WordPress (advanced) • SharePoint (working) …”
- Keep punctuation consistent and avoid overloading this line with implementation skills already covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution”; consider merging or differentiating one section.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent NACo roles, so this item should add nuance, not just restate the platform names.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, this section should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic front-end terms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw languages to applied capability: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping versioned/basic terms (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the role targets hands-on developer screening; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add specificity tied to recent work: e.g., “custom Drupal front-end implementation,” “analytics/tag deployment,” or “workflow/deployment automation.”
- Order by relevance/modernity: JavaScript • API integrations • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • Google Tag Manager • HTML/CSS • jQuery

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- GTM may fit better under Analytics/Optimization if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more differentiated.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize systems you actively build with, not general collaboration apps.
- Suggested rewrite: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello**  
- If accurate, strengthen label to: **Automation, Workflow & Project Systems**
- Best upgrade: add one short qualifier elsewhere or in a summary line, e.g. “Built cross-team workflow systems and automations for editorial planning, approvals and reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Slack and Teams are generic communication tools; they add little value here and dilute the automation focus.
- Basecamp overlaps with Jira/Asana/Trello as project management software; consider dropping it unless it was a primary platform in recent roles.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Because recent roles already emphasize email leadership, this item should stay concise and signal enterprise-level CRM/marketing automation relevance.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely strategic weight/relevance: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, sharpen phrasing to reflect use case: **CRM-based email automation, member communications and newsletter operations**
- Optional stronger version: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | Email automation, audience segmentation, newsletter distribution**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding claims here like “managed newsletters reaching tens of thousands” since that already appears in Work Experience.
- Don’t repeat broader “multi-channel communications” language; keep this item tool-specific to complement the stronger experience bullets.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and repeats analytics platforms already proven in the recent Director role. Tighten it to emphasize methods and decision-making value, not just software names.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • KPI design • Dashboard development • SEO analysis • A/B testing**
- Replace vague **“Dashboarding”** with **“Dashboard development”** or **“Executive reporting”** for a more professional, outcome-oriented phrasing.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this skill set to impact in recent roles with metrics (e.g., reporting for **3.5M annual page views**, **10,000+ page** platform, **50+ publishers**) rather than adding more tools here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills [3] Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider merging or making one more strategic and this one purely technical.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the **Director of Digital Media** entry, so avoid repeating the exact same list multiple times.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and anchor it in “firsts,” production volume, or workflow improvements.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout and hands-on delivery: “Promoted through two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten phrasing and reduce channel list sprawl: “improved workflows across web, email, social and video” instead of “strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: website refresh scale, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, production cadence, or team size supported.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted through two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social and video. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates. Provided day-to-day oversight for a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the format, not expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; frame this as foundational support rather than leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the launch and scope, and trim broad support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and tighten phrasing: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a more specific verb/outcome if possible: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If you can quantify, add scale: number of episodes, audience, departments supported, or project outputs.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid overplaying multimedia leadership here; later roles already show stronger video/digital ownership.
- “Supporting organizational programs and policy work” is vague and may repeat broader communications language elsewhere unless made more specific.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills, so this section should stay tool-focused and concise.

Suggested edit:
- Retitle or tighten to emphasize tools, not functions: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator”
- If you want to keep capabilities, separate them cleanly: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream studio operations • Podcast production”
- Use consistent naming with other technical items; spell out Adobe products for polish and ATS clarity.
- Only keep capability terms here if they reflect current, hands-on work; otherwise let recent experience carry the impact.
